notes: The appendix table of the 1990 UMB context statement, “UMBs and Historic Ratings by Study Area” — 51 PDF pages of fixed-column rows covering all eleven study areas, one row per unreinforced masonry building. Each row gives a street number and street, a building-prototype letter, the assessor's block and lot, the assessor's year, and eight columns of 1990 rating codes keyed on PDF pages 159–163. The YEAR column is the assessor's own and the key says so, so it is recorded as check material and never published as a construction date. The document's 200 inventory forms are the sibling batch `umb-survey`.

coverage.remaining: Nothing of this table. About 100 rows on five pages are lost to the scan rather than unread: pages 367 and 419 lost their street-number column outright (32 and 23 rows), and pages 169, 223 and 251 lost it on a few rows each. They are recoverable only by re-OCRing those page images — macOS Vision is available on this machine and no OCR engine is installed otherwise.
coverage.note: All 51 PDF pages of the appendix table read, reconstructed from pdftotext -bbox-layout word coordinates rather than line text. 1,902 rows carry a street number and enough of a row to identify a building; 1,097 carry a Heritage rating, 325 a historic district, 295 a 1976 citywide survey rating, 37 a City Landmark marking. 1,715 print an assessor's block and 1,406 a lot, which is what tested every resolution.
